State 2: Call the event helper at $A02E; the following describes the path when it returns here. Copy $1B17,X to the working byte at $A074, read the table at $A076 indexed by $1AF5,X, call the frame helper at $A01E, then increment the index and replace values of 4 or above with 0. The table is read before the bound check. Decrement $1AD3,X. If its result is nonnegative, pass A=4 to $4574 when the working byte is negative or $45BC otherwise; return if the callback result AND 6 equals 2. Otherwise set $1AD3,X to $FF, toggle bit 7 of $1B17,X, set the state to 3 and return. The event helper, incoming index range and natural reachability remain open.

State 3: Call the event helper at $A02E; the following describes the path when it returns here. Copy $1B17,X to the working byte at $A074, read the table at $A076 indexed by $1AF5,X, call the frame helper at $A01E, then increment the index and replace values of 4 or above with 0. The table is read before the bound check. Decrement $1AD3,X. If its result is nonnegative, pass A=4 to $4574 when the working byte is negative or $45BC otherwise; return if the callback result AND 6 equals 2. Otherwise set the state to 0 and return. The event helper, incoming index range and natural reachability remain open.

State 4 decrements $1AC2,X with eight-bit wrap. A negative result copies $1AE4,X into $1AB1,X and returns. Otherwise call $72FC, pass A=8 to $4574 on set carry or $45BC on clear carry, then mask the callback’s returned A with 6. If the result is 2, return without changing the state; otherwise copy $1AE4,X into $1AB1,X. Natural reachability and external callbacks remain open.

State 5 decrements $1AC2,X with eight-bit wrap. If the result is negative, call $4B0E with A=$50 and jump to $5DB9 with A=$14. Otherwise copy $1B17,X to the working byte at $A074, read the table at $A07A indexed by $1AD3,X, and call the frame helper at $A01E. Increment the index with eight-bit wrap; if it is at least 4, replace it with 0, then store it back to $1AD3,X. The table read occurs before this bound check, so the possible incoming index range remains open.

Test the sign of the working byte at $A074. If negative, clear carry and add 6 to A. Then clear carry again, add $19E5,X, store the low byte at $19C3,X and return. This binary arithmetic assumes decimal mode is clear; overflow from the first addition does not carry into the second.
Working byte tested with BIT by the frame helper. Several handler paths write $1B17,X here; its value differs among the captured snapshots.
Four captured frame offsets 2, 2, 0, 0. The state-2 and state-3 paths index these with $1AF5,X and call the frame helper at $A01E; the index has no local bound.
Four captured frame offsets 4, 4, 2, 2. The state-5 path indexes these with $1AD3,X and calls the frame helper at $A01E; the index has no local bound.
